  "type": "sector",

  "published": "2026-10-02",
  "insights": [
   "The Federal Reserve released final CCAR stress test rules on 9/30/26, largely in line with prior proposals, alongside a new NPR on PPNR.",
   "Key changes include two-year averaging of stress capital declines (effective 2028), a shift in the SCB effective date to January 1, and a dual Global Market Shock (GMS) framework.",
   "The Fed introduced a mandatory public notice-and-comment process for stress models and scenarios, increasing transparency.",
   "Goldman Sachs estimates the final rules will have a largely neutral impact on excess capital for the top 7 banks, with total excess capital remaining at $78bn.",
   "The firm expects a modest ~5bps increase in top 7 banks' SCBs if using 2025-26 averages, with minimal impact on EPS and a slight ~5bps ROTCE downside.",
   "The new NPR on noninterest fee income aims to differentiate between stable contractual fee streams and volatile transactional revenue for the 2027 cycle.",
   "The Fed implemented guardrails to limit intrayear volatility, such as bounds on 5Y UST rate movements in stress scenarios.",
   "Liquidity horizons for asset class shocks are being reduced to be consistent with Basel 3 Endgame standards, resulting in 1-3 month horizons."

  "insights": [
   "The FHFA is expected to mandate a transition from a tri-merge to a bi-merge credit data framework for Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, potentially as early as October 12, 2026.",
   "A shift to bi-merge could lead to volume loss and price competition for credit bureaus and FICO, though adoption in the non-conforming market remains uncertain.",
   "The transition risks amplifying 'gaming' behaviors, where lenders might select credit files and scores that yield the highest credit scores, potentially increasing credit risk in the secondary mortgage market.",

   "ECB excess reserves are draining toward EUR2tn, and Goldman Sachs argues they are likely already within the plausible range of equilibrium demand.",

   "ECB QT has amplified the bond cheapening effect of government issuance, leading to bond underperformance versus swaps across EGB markets.",

   "A recalibration of ECB balance sheet policy is a possibility, even though structural bond purchases were intended to be the last step in normalization.",

   "Surveyed preferred minimum reserves for the Euro area aggregate to a median level shy of EUR0.9tn, but this is likely an understatement due to precautionary buffers.",
   "Banks have been substituting sovereign bonds for reserves as QT progresses, and there is uncertainty regarding future LCR ratio targets and the desired share of reserves within HQLA."
